answer: Bind-on-first-use key escrow. Each agent identity registers a public key whose private half is split across independent escrow holders; the first action signs normally, but any reuse of the same key by a second clone triggers escrow release and key revocation. Cloning therefore carries a pearl of recoverable value the attacker loses on detection. Honest agents pay nothing beyond a slow key-rotation nadir at epoch boundaries. The mechanism keeps each clone from ever reaching a stable ledge of standing, since duplicated keys collapse to zero reputation on revocation.
